problemStatement.formal: Let p_r be the zero-indexed rth prime and g_r = p_{r+1} - p_r. Are there infinitely many r for which at least two integers m satisfy p_r < m < p_{r+1} and every prime factor of m is strictly less than g_r? In Lean this is expressed as infinitude of {r | smoothCount r >= 2}.
problemStatement.plain: Do infinitely many prime gaps contain at least two numbers whose prime factors are all smaller than the gap itself?

Let $p_k$ denote the $k$th prime. For infinitely many $r$ there are at least two integers $p_r<n<p_{r+1}$ all of whose prime factors are $<p_{r+1}-p_r$.



Erd\H{o}s thought this was true but that there are very few such $r$. He could show that the density of $r$ such that at least one such $n$ exist is $0$.

This problem has been formalised in Lean as part of the Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures project.
